name: Kevin White
priorities: Supporting bird-friendly habitat (e.g. planting/protecting trees and native plants, protecting   waterways, increasing greenspaces), Implementing environmental impact studies for development applications, Helping developers and communities to learn more about keeping Kitchener's birds healthy and safe, Considering policy or resources to address the environmental impacts of rodenticide and cosmetic herbicide, I admit my ignorance on the specifics of several of these issues, so I may well wish to pursue them, but I cannot honestly endorse things I have such limited knowledge of. I can say that should these issues be presented before council, the primary consideration would be the core value of care for people and the land we share (and the land does indeed include birds).
platform: Again, adhering to the core value of care for people and the land we share, this includes land shared with birds and all other things living on it.
favourite: Tough question. I've always liked seeing Herons in Waterloo Park, standing in the water. My favourite bird is probably an ostrich, though. Or maybe a chicken. I think they move in delightful ways. My grandfather always liked red-winged blackbirds, so I have a soft spot for them, too, but I also had the back of my head/bike helmet pecked repeatedly by one when I went biking on a path and they had nested nearby. So, I'm not sure what they think of me. I think we're okay, though.
extra: I really do believe that the Region of Waterloo has stated an excellent core value: care for people and the land we share. That requires us to be in relationship with each other and the land. It also requires our elected representatives to be accountable for their decisions, and they should be able to clearly indicate that this value is being implemented in all their decisions. So whether we're discussing birds, fish, greenspace, corporate development, or anything else, the first consideration should always be how it impacts and supports people and the land. It is my hope that through persistent commitment to this, communities and community partners whom we serve and work with will also emphasize this core value in the work they do.

platform: Protecting and expanding Kitchener’s urban tree canopy, natural areas, wetlands, and connected green spaces. A bird-friendly city is also a healthy city for people; and I strongly advocate for the respect of all aspects of our Earth for now and future generation. I want to support thoughtful development that protects important habitats while creating more native plantings, pollinator-friendly spaces, and safe green corridors throughout our neighbourhoods.
favourite: The Northern Cardinal. I love its bright red colour and distinctive song, but I also appreciate how familiar and resilient it is. They also carry spiritual significance for me personally. I love to hear everyone's personal, familial, spiritual, academic and cultural appreciations of our environment. Cardinals are a reminder that nature can be part of our everyday lives, even in a growing city. Creating neighbourhoods with mature trees, native plants, and healthy green spaces helps ensure that birds like the cardinal continue to thrive alongside us.
extra: I believe good city-building means thinking about the long term. The choices we make about housing, transportation, parks, trees, and natural spaces today will shape Kitchener for generations. I want to help build a city that is welcoming, sustainable, and resilient—a place where people can afford to live, businesses can thrive. I will work to ensure all aspects of our Earth are respected, cared for, enjoyed, and overall remains an important part of our everyday lives.

platform: A key part of my platform is to close the parkland deficit in Ward 10. Closing the parkland deficit in Ward 10 isn't just good for families, it creates essential green stepping stones and native plant habitat for urban birdlife right in our core. But because Ward 10 is growing so fast with high-density towers, we also need to address window collisions. I support requiring bird-safe glass standards and dark-sky lighting guidelines on new high-rise builds along King Street so our density growth doesn't come at the expense of local wildlife.
favourite: I am a big fan of crows. I had a few friendly crows who lived outside the last place I lived. They would perch in the tree in my front lawn and I would talk to them every day. I provided food and water for the neighborhood birds and the crows took notice.
extra: Long-term solutions require all levels of government working together, but progress happens when each level stays focused on its core job. As your Councillor for Ward 10, my daily priority is managing what City Hall actually controls: directing high-density growth responsibly, protecting public assets, expanding green space, and keeping our streets safe and vibrant.

platform: The most bird-friendly part of my platform is my prioritization of smart and sustainable growth. Sustainable growth considers climate impacts, environmental challenges and effects to local wildlife. The Region of Waterloo can implement educational programs which promote bird-friendly policies to the general public and vote in favour of public policies which consider bird-friendly actions (e.g., reducing light pollution and increasing habitat).
favourite: My favourite bird species is the Blue Heron (Ardea herodias).  I attribute it to fond memories as a child walking along the Grand River near the Cambridge Mill. I loved how long, majestic, and peaceful it looked both standing in the water and when it would fly away. I also appreciated it's patience while hunting for food, so calm and still. Every time I see one my excitement for it is still the same as a when I was a child, and now I get to share that with my children on our walks in the Huron Natural Area.
extra: The Region of Waterloo is feeling the effects of climate change. All development needs to consider its impact to our environment. As a Regional Councillor, I will champion projects that appropriately include green initiatives and use innovative design to reduce environmental impact.

name: Vikki Poirier
priorities: Supporting bird-friendly habitat (e.g. planting/protecting trees and native plants, protecting   waterways, increasing greenspaces), Supporting bird-friendly development and zoning by-laws (e.g. reducing light pollution, window treatments)), Implementing environmental impact studies for development applications, Helping developers and communities to learn more about keeping Kitchener's birds healthy and safe, Considering policy or resources to address Kitchener's (Waterloo Region's) free-roaming and/or feral cats
platform: The most bird-friendly part of my platform is protecting Ward 4’s green spaces and strengthening environmental resilience. From the trails and natural areas around Doon South and Brigadoon to Strasburg Creek and the Homer Watson Park area, Ward 4 has important natural spaces and wildlife habitat. As our neighbourhoods grow, we need to protect these areas, preserve our tree canopy and ensure development is environmentally responsible.
favourite: My favourite bird is the crow. They’re incredibly intelligent, adaptable, and resourceful—and maybe a little misunderstood. I appreciate their ability to problem-solve, look out for one another, and adapt to whatever is happening around them. There’s something about that resilience and determination that I really admire.
extra:
I believe protecting our environment starts locally—in our neighbourhoods, parks, trails and backyards. As Ward 4 continues to grow, I want to be thoughtful about what we build and what we protect.
Good leadership also means listening, learning and asking questions. I won’t pretend to be an expert on every issue, but I will listen to residents and experts, follow the evidence, and advocate for practical solutions.
Because a growing Ward 4 should still be a place where people—and crows—can thrive.

Blue Jays!

When I was in elementary school, a pair of Blue Jays built a nest right outside our classroom window. They became our official class pets. priorities: Supporting bird-friendly habitat (e.g. planting/protecting trees and native plants, protecting   waterways, increasing greenspaces), Supporting bird-friendly development and zoning by-laws (e.g. reducing light pollution, window treatments)), Implementing environmental impact studies for development applications, Reducing public or commercial window collisions by implementing collision risk assessments for public facilities, Ensuring environmental considerations, including bird-friendly design and habitat protection, are integrated into infrastructure, growth and development decisions from the beginning.
platform: Protecting the natural systems that make Waterloo Region such a special place to live. As our community grows, I believe growth and environmental stewardship have to go hand in hand. That means protecting our water, wetlands and natural areas, supporting responsible land-use planning, and making decisions that consider biodiversity and climate resilience. Healthy habitats for birds are also healthy communities for people.
favourite:
There are two: 
1. My Caribbean pick would be the Magnificent Frigatebird. They’re such a striking part of the Caribbean landscape, and I love how they soar effortlessly above the water. My mother is from Antigua and it also symbolic for freedom, resilience and soaring above challenges.

2. My Canadian pick would be the Canada Jay. It’s resilient, resourceful and distinctly Canadian, it can thrive even in some of our harshest environments.
extra: Waterloo Region is growing, and the choices we make today will shape what kind of community we leave to the next generation. I believe we don't have to choose between growth, affordability and protecting our environment. Good planning means considering all three. I will continue listening to residents, using evidence to guide decisions, and working to ensure Waterloo Region remains a healthy, welcoming and sustainable place for people and wildlife alike.

platform: The most bird-friendly stance I take is blocking AI data centers in not just Ward 10 but all city limits of Kitchener. Data centers create continuous noise that disrupts bird communication, heavy night lighting that disorients migratory birds, and massive water consumption that depletes local wetland habitats. Protecting our water table and keeping downtown focused on green, human-centered development keeps Kitchener a true Bird Friendly City.

extra: I will never give or break on data centers. Protecting our groundwater supply through strict industrial zoning ensures that local natural systems such as Victoria Park, Schneider Creek, and the Grand River watershed maintain the water levels needed to sustain native insects, aquatic life, and bird habitats.

name: Aalaa Rehman
priorities: Supporting bird-friendly habitat (e.g. planting/protecting trees and native plants, protecting   waterways, increasing greenspaces), Supporting bird-friendly development and zoning by-laws (e.g. reducing light pollution, window treatments)), Implementing environmental impact studies for development applications, Helping developers and communities to learn more about keeping Kitchener's birds healthy and safe, Reducing public or commercial window collisions by implementing collision risk assessments for public facilities, Considering policy or resources to address the environmental impacts of rodenticide and cosmetic herbicide
platform:
One of the four core pillars of my campaign is my commitment to sustainability and protecting green space as Kitchener grows. I believe we should be building neighbourhoods that are not only affordable and walkable for people, but also healthy and resilient for the wildlife that shares our city.

I support continuing to protect and expand our tree canopy. I support planting more of species native to this area. I will suport preserving important habitats and waterways, and considering the environmental impacts of development from the beginning rather than only as an afterthought. I also want to see us think more carefully about how buildings affect wildlife, including bird collisions with windows and the impacts of unnecessary light pollution.

As we work to provide more housing and fill these deficits, environmental stewardship needs to be part of the planning process at every stage. Parks and natural spaces are not simply amenities; they contribute to climate resilience (an essentiality as we can see with how every year climate catastrophes ramp up and our air quality becomes worse in Ontario with the fires) and the long-term health of our neighbourhoods. Also, it's important to consider general community well-being, of which greenspace naturally lends itself to.
favourite: My favorite bird species is the mourning dove! My mother has always loved them, and so she passed that appreciation onto me.
extra: Please visit my website for more information about me! aalaaconseil.org

As Kitchener grows, we should ensure that development considers local biodiversity and that our parks and natural areas remain healthy for wildlife
favourite: Penguins! I've always loved penguins because of their unique personalities, fascinating adaptations, and the way they work together to survive in challenging environments. They're also a reminder of how important it is to protect wildlife and the ecosystems animals depend on, particularly as climate change affects habitats around the world.

From protecting green spaces and planting native trees to making thoughtful decisions about development, I believe we have a responsibility to preserve our natural environment for future generations. And, of course, I think the world could always use a little more appreciation for penguins🐧!
